title: The Singhs Ravage Lahore and Turn Toward Imnabad

blocks.text: After striking at Mughal camps and slipping away with horses, the Singhs widened their raids until they laid waste around Lahore and made the highways unsafe for imperial traffic. They fought while vastly outnumbered, then vanished again into brush, marsh, and broken ground before the larger forces could trap them.

The page stresses how poor the Khalsa still was at this stage: they had no stores, weapons, clothing, or money fit for a settled kingdom. Their only wealth was faith in the Guru's word, and that conviction kept them moving even when hunger, wounds, and exhaustion would have broken ordinary soldiers.

From that hard experience the narrative draws a political lesson as well as a military one. The Singhs begin reasoning that without forts, war could not be sustained for long, so they look beyond mere raiding and turn their attention toward richer districts such as Imnabad, where supplies and durable strength might be seized.
